Lowering one’s gaze (*al-busru*) is encouraged in certain contexts (e.g., avoiding inappropriate glances at others, especially those not *mahram*—non-family members of the opposite gender). - However, **simply looking down out of arrogance or disrespect** (e.g., ignoring coworkers, acting superior) is contrary to Islamic values. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: > *"The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, but there is good in everyone as long as he fears Allah."* (Muslim) - Humility (*khushu’*) is praised, but it should not be confused with disdain or rudeness. 2. **Behavior in Public & Workplace:** - Islam encourages **modesty in speech and actions** (*haya*). If John is looking down due to shyness or discomfort, that is understandable. However, if it’s due to **arrogance or indifference**, it would be frowned upon. - The Prophet (ﷺ) said: > *"The believer has a heart, and faith is a light in it. When one is upright, it shines; but when one is crooked, it dims."* (Al-Tirmidhi) - A true believer should strive for balance—neither arrogance nor excessive humility (which can border on rudeness). 3. **Intent (*Niyyah*) Matters:** - Islam places great importance on **intent**. If John is looking down because he is **shy, focused, or avoiding unnecessary attention**, that is acceptable. But if he is doing so out of **pride or disrespect**, it would be wrong. - The Prophet (ﷺ) said: > *"Actions are judged by intentions, and each person will get what he intended."* (Bukhari) ### **Conclusion (General Islamic View):** - **Not inherently wrong** if done with good intent (e.g., modesty, focus). - **Wrong if done with arrogance or disrespect**—Islam encourages **balanced humility and respect** in all interactions.
